title: Phased deployment governor and safety fences for model variants
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a "phased deployment governor" service and config surface that declaratively expresses staged traffic shifts, shadowing/A-B branches, and automatic rollback fences for model variant promotions. The governor will: validate rollout configs at creation time, simulate expected traffic distributions, enforce runtime traffic splits and step schedules, evaluate guardrail rules against live metrics (latency, error-rate, degradation delta, quality regressions), and trigger safe automated rollback or pause actions. This ticket scopes the core config model, validation engine, runtime enforcer hooks, and Console integration for visible rollout controls and actions.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can create a phased rollout manifest describing stages (percent, duration) and multiple target variants (primary, shadow, experiment) via API and Console.
The governor validates manifests: percent totals, non-overlapping phases, and rejects incompatible scheduling (e.g., >100% sum, negative durations).
A rollout simulation endpoint returns expected per-minute traffic split and estimated cost delta for a given manifest.
At runtime the enforcer applies traffic splits and shadow forwarding with <5ms added median latency for routing decisions under load.
Guardrails evaluate three configurable signals (p99 latency, error-rate, eval-quality metric) and will automatically pause or roll back to previous stable variant when thresholds are breached.
Console shows per-stage progress, a timeline of applied percentages, and exposes a single-click abort/rollforward action; actions are recorded in audit logs.
End-to-end tests simulate an injection of errors and demonstrate automatic rollback behavior in the staging environment.
Documentation in the model-lifecycle repo explains schema, examples for A/B experiments, shadow-only runs, and team runbooks for manual overrides.
design_notes: Favor a compact manifest DSL instead of a full policy language for V1 to reduce cognitive load (phases: [{percent,duration,traffic_target}]).
We will support both percentage-based and token-based split targets later; tokens deferred to follow-up (dependency noted).
Guardrails will be configurable per-rollout with default conservative thresholds for P0 customers; thresholds are stored as part of the manifest metadata.
Tradeoff: pushing complex decision logic into the governor centralizes safety but increases blast radius; mitigate by scoped RBAC and canarying the governor itself.
Simulation runs are approximate and assume steady-state traffic distributions; include disclaimer in Console for bursty traffic patterns.
implementation_plan: Schema: create JSON schema v1 for phased rollout manifests and validation rules. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-lifecycle/pull/122)
API: add POST /rollouts (create), GET /rollouts/:id/simulate, PATCH /rollouts/:id/actions. Draft in runtime router service.
Enforcer: runtime router plugin that reads active rollout config and atomically swaps traffic weights in the routing table with metrics-tagged tokens.
Guardrail evaluator: streaming metrics consumer (kafka->enforcer) that evaluates thresholds and writes actions to the rollout audit log and control topic.
Console: new rollout details page with timeline chart, simulation tool, and Abort/Rollforward buttons.
E2E tests: end-to-end in staging with synthetic workload generator and chaos injection to validate automatic rollback.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest validation and schema edge cases.
Integration tests for enforcer plugin under concurrent requests (load test target: 10k rps per node).
Staging e2e test that simulates quality regression and confirms governor triggers rollback within configured SLA.
Manual QA session for Console UX with Solutions Engineering and two customer personas: platform team and product engineer.
metrics_and_slo: Routing decision latency: median < 5ms, p99 < 25ms when under typical load.
Rollback detection window: guardrails must detect regressions and emit an action within configured stage duration or 5 minutes whichever is smaller.
False rollback rate in staging must be <1% for default thresholds during validation period.
observability_hooks: Emit rollout lifecycle events to telemetry (rollout.started, stage.applied, guardrail.triggered, rollout.aborted, rollout.completed).
Tag traces with rollout_id and variant_id to correlate latency/error spikes to rollout stages.
Expose a Console dashboard tile that surfaces current active rollouts, their stage progress, and last guardrail evaluation result.
